texts.full_text: CL 400.607; MSA 16.614(7). After a preliminary examination in Detroit Recorder's Court, examining magistrate Clarence Laster, Jr., dismissed the indictment. The prosecution applied for an order of superintending control in the Wayne County Circuit Court. Chief Judge Richard D. Dunn granted the order, directing Judge Laster to vacate the dismissal and bind the defendant over for trial. Proceedings have been stayed pending this appeal from Judge Dunn's order. The issue in the case centers on the applicability of the grand jury provision in Michigan's constitution and whether the prosecution can use both a grand jury indictment and a preliminary examination to bind a defendant over for trial. The pertinent facts are as follows: The defendant was originally charged with Medicaid fraud via a grand jury indictment. A preliminary examination was subsequently held, and the magistrate dismissed the indictment, finding that the prosecution had not met its burden of proof. The prosecution then sought an order of superintending control to reinstate the charges. The defendant argues that the use of both a grand jury indictment and a preliminary examination violates the constitutional provision against double jeopardy. The prosecution contends that the grand jury indictment and the preliminary examination serve different purposes and that the use of both is not prohibited. The Michigan Constitution of 1963, art 1, § 14, provides: "No person shall be held to answer for a capital or otherwise infamous crime unless on a presentment or indictment of a grand jury except in cases arising in the land or naval forces, or in the militia, when in actual service in time of war

Due to their large size and ease of study, major ampullate (MA) glands have received the most attention. Previous diffraction studies have been done on dragline silk indicate that the MA silk is a semicrystalline biopolymer composed of crystalline domains consisting of [unreadable]-(L-polyalanine) sheets embedded in a glycine rich amorphous matrix [4-6]. Comparatively little isknown about the minor ampullate (MiA) silk, which is responsible for capturing prey and strengthening the web. Recent findings confirm that MiA silk is not a semicrystalline polymer, but with a similar crystal structure compared to MA silk [7]. ile it may not seem that empty elements contain useful information, they can alter the layout of a document given appropriate styling. This directive is most useful when you are processing machine-generated HTML, please avoid using it on regular user HTML.

Elements that contain only whitespace will be treated as empty. Non-breaking spaces, however, do not count as whitespace. See %AutoFormat.RemoveEmpty.RemoveNbsp for alternate behavior.

This algorithm is not perfect; you may still notice some empty tags, particularly if a node had elements, but those elements were later removed because they were not permitted in that context, or tags that, after being auto-closed by another tag, where empty. This is for safety reasons to prevent clever code from breaking validation. The general rule of thumb: if a tag looked empty on the way in, it will get removed; if HTML Purifier made it empty, it will stay.

--# vim: et sw=4 sts=4

To date, although the InGaN based blue LDs are already commercialized and the material growth technology has been significantly improved, the factors to achieve optimal optoelectronic performance have not been fully developed. There are still many places that need attention for further research. Among these areas of interest is understanding how quantum confinement effects impact laser efficiency in InGaN-based MQW structures and exploring methods to improve electron-hole overlap within the wells, as this directly affects emission properties \[[@B11-micromachines-10-00875]\]. Additionally, issues such as strain-induced defects due to lattice mismatch between GaN layers can degrade performance. Therefore addressing these challenges through material engineering techniques or improved growth conditions is critical. Furthermore, achieving high output power and stable operation at elevated temperatures remains a hurdle for InGaN-based LDs \[[@B12-micromachines-10-00875]\]. Various strategies have been proposed to mitigate thermal effects on laser diodes; however no single solution has yet proven sufficient across all use cases. For instance, improving the heat dissipation of device structures or refining substrate materials and their bonding techniques may contribute significantly toward this goal \[[@B13-micromachines-10-00875]\]. Another essential aspect that requires further investigation is developing reliable fabrication processes for these laser diodes while maintaining cost-effectiveness in mass production settings. While some advances have been made, scalability remains challenging due to complex multilayer structures necessary within InGaN MQWs \[[@B14-micromachines-10-00875]\]. Finally as full-color display technology continues advancing it is imperative for laser manufacturers like the ones discussed above who develop blue and green LDs that red emission capabilities be incorporated without sacrificing performance or dramatically increasing production costs. Research in achieving effective tunable white-light emissions from single chip-based InGaN structures will thus also remain an active field of interest moving forward \[[@B15-micromachines-10-00875]\].
